name: Spell out zero through nine in prose

source.quote: Prose, 0 through 9: The word (five projects). Prose, 10 and up: Numeral. Measurements and durations: Numeral, even below 10.

message: In prose, counts below 10 are words. Numerals stay for measurements, durations, times, versions, percentages, identifiers, and when a sentence mixes numbers of the same kind above and below 10.

pass: The release has 14 fixes, 3 new features, and 2 known issues.

name: Never start a sentence with a numeral

source.quote: Start of a sentence: Never a numeral. Spell it out or rewrite. Eleven projects are active.

message: A sentence that opens with a digit is easy to misread as a list number or a continuation.
fix: Spell the number out, or rewrite so it isn't first.

pass: The team has 11 active projects. 2026 was a busy year.

name: Percent in prose, % in UI and tables

source.quote: Percent in prose: Numeral plus percent (50 percent). Percent in UI and tables: Numeral plus % (Resolved: 87%).

message: In running text the guide spells out "percent". The symbol is for UI strings and tables.

pass: About 50 percent of tasks are overdue.

name: Use % in tables

source.quote: Percent in UI and tables: Numeral plus %.

message: Tables have tight space, so the guide uses the symbol there.

name: Space between a number and its unit

source.quote: Put a space between a number and its unit: 25 MB, 5 GB, 30 ms. No space before a percent sign: 87%.

message: The unit is a separate word, and the percent sign is not.
fix: Write "25 MB" and "30 ms". In running text, write a percentage as "87 percent".

pass: The file is larger than 25 MB.

name: Spell out the month in dates

source.quote: Spell out the month. 6/12/2026 means two different dates depending on the reader's country. Write June 12, 2026.

message: A numeric date reads differently in different countries. ISO dates belong in data formats, logs, and code.

name: No ordinals in dates

source.quote: Don't use ordinals in dates. June 1, not June 1st.

message: The ordinal suffix adds nothing to a date.

name: Name a month or quarter, not a season

source.quote: Name a month or a quarter, not a season. Seasons differ by hemisphere.

message: A season names different months in each hemisphere.
fix: Name the month or the quarter: "in March" or "in Q1 2027".

name: Time of day with AM or PM

source.quote: Time of day: Numeral plus AM or PM, or 24-hour time if the product uses it. 10:45 AM, or 22:45. Write noon and midnight, not 12:00.

message: The guide writes times as a numeral, a space, and AM or PM in capitals. Noon and midnight are written as words.

name: Don't put from before an en dash range

source.quote: In prose, write from 5 through 50. Don't put from before an en dash range.

fix: Write "from 5 through 50" or "10:00 AM to 2:00 PM".

name: Ranges in prose use words

source.quote: In prose, write from 5 through 50. In tables and UI, use an en dash with no spaces: 2016–2026. For times, use to: 10:00 AM to 2:00 PM.

message: In running text the guide spells out ranges. The en dash form is for tables and UI, where space is tight.

pass: Wait 5 to 10 minutes before you retry.

name: Commas in numbers from four digits

source.quote: Use a comma from four digits: 1,024. Don't use one in years (2026), after a decimal point, or in version numbers, port numbers, and identifiers (port 8080).

message: A plain number of five or more digits is hard to read without separators. Years, versions, ports, and identifiers are exempt, and this check can't always tell them apart, so it only suggests. Four-digit numbers are skipped because most are years.
fix: Write "10,000" if it's a quantity. Leave an identifier, port, or version as it is.

name: Name the currency

source.quote: Name the currency: 25 USD, or US$25.

message: Several countries use the dollar sign, and other currencies share symbols too.

pass: The plan costs 25 USD a month.
The plan costs US$25 a month.

name: Join key names with a plus sign and no spaces

source.quote: Keys and shortcuts: Key names as printed on the keyboard, joined by a plus sign with no spaces. Press Ctrl+S (Windows and Linux) or Cmd+S (macOS).

message: Key names are written as printed on the keyboard and joined by a plus sign with no spaces.

pass: Press Ctrl+S (Windows and Linux) or Cmd+S (macOS).

name: HTTP methods in capitals

source.quote: Write the HTTP method in capitals and the path in code style: GET /projects/{id}.

message: The method is a protocol token, so it's written in capitals.
fix: Write "GET /projects/{id}" and put the path in code style.

name: In a dialog, on a tab

source.quote: dialog, pane, list, box, window: in. tab, page, menu, toolbar: on.

message: The guide pairs each UI element with one preposition so instructions read the same everywhere.
fix: Write "in the dialog" and "on the Sharing tab".

flag: In the Sharing tab, select Invite people.
pass: On the Sharing tab, select Invite people.

name: Choose a or an by sound

source.quote: Choose a or an by sound: an API, an SSO setting, a URL, an HTML file.

message: The article depends on how the acronym is said aloud, not on its first letter.
fix: Write "an API", "an SSO setting", "a URL", "an HTML file".
